title: Warm Japanese Barley Noodles
description: A savory Japanese dish featuring self-raising flour and pressure-cooked barley, perfect for a weeknight dinner. This egg-free-friendly meal is a great option for those with dietary restrictions.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the self-raising flour and 1/2 cup of water to form a smooth dough.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until it becomes elastic.
Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces and roll each piece into a long rope.
Cut the rope into 1/4 inch thick slices to form the noodles.
In a large pot, combine the barley and 4 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes or until the barley is tender.
In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sesame oil to make the sauce.
In a large pan, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat and cook the noodles for 2-3 minutes or until they are lightly browned.
Add the cooked barley and sauce to the pan and stir to combine.
Cook for an additional 2 minutes or until the noodles are well coated with the sauce.
Garnish with green onions and serve hot.
